reason: E1 directly supports the premise that nanoscale Cu precipitates below domain wall thickness do not deteriorate coercivity, which is central to the mechanism. However, E1 provides no evidence for the other key premises: the specific behavior of Cu in MnNiSi alloys, the ability of rapid solidification to produce the required precipitate dispersion, or the baseline mechanical/magnetocaloric properties of MnNiSi. These are assumed without citation.
premises: Cu nano-precipitates below domain wall thickness do not increase coercivity
Nanoscale precipitates can strengthen via Orowan mechanism
Rapid solidification can produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates in MnNiSi
MnNiSi-based alloys have large magnetocaloric effect but poor mechanical performance
Microstructural barriers that impede dislocations also pin magnetic domain walls
